I have been farming these 40 mu in Quzhou for 6 years now. I never went to school, so everything I know I learned by doing it myself and watching Old Wang and the others around me. Last year my wheat made about 500-some jin per mu and my maize made over 600 jin. This year I will do about the same — maybe a little more fertilizer — because cutting back is too risky. On 40 mu I can handle wasting some fertilizer, but a bad harvest means real trouble.

For wheat, I plant in October. After the maize comes out, I hire the rotary tiller to go over the field. I buy the improved wheat seed from the same dealer as my neighbors — I do not know the exact name, but it is the same kind everyone here plants. For base fertilizer, I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that is 100 jin. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, and at heading I put another 20 jin of urea. That is about 40 jin of urea total per mu. I irrigate four times from the well: winter water, green-up water, jointing water, and one more when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide three times, mainly for aphids and rust. I expect around 550 kg per mu if the weather is decent.

For maize, after we cut the wheat in early June there is no time to plough. I plant hybrid maize seed directly into the wheat stubble — no-tillage. I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the dealer recommends, the same one my neighbors plant. At planting I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the row. When the maize gets to big trumpet stage, I spread half a bag of urea per mu. I irrigate three times — seedling stage, big trumpet, and filling stage. The well never runs dry, so water is not a problem. I spray pesticide three times for corn borer and armyworm. I expect about 650 kg per mu.

With 40 mu, I have to buy a lot of bags at once. It costs me thousands of yuan, but I can manage it. I always tell myself: better a bit too much fertilizer than too little. I watch what my neighbors do, and if they all do about the same, then I do it too. Changing what worked last year is dangerous.
